raw_response:
I’m farming only 4.1 mu, and there are just two of us at home, with some off-farm work, so I can’t spread myself too thin. I still keep the wheat-maize rotation on most of the land because that is the steadiest way for me to have income through the year, and I leave a smaller piece for cotton since I know how to manage it and cotton can still bring cash if the price is acceptable. I finished middle school, so I do listen when people talk about rates and timing, but in the end I still go by what worked on my own fields. Last year, wheat and maize were still the safest on our better land, and cotton I keep on a smaller patch because it takes more picking labor. Fertilizer is expensive, so I won’t chase very high rates, but I also don’t want the crop to look weak. I’d rather use a moderate amount, split it where it matters, and save some cash for irrigation and pest control. Since I have well water, I can keep wheat safer with two or three irrigations if spring is dry. Maize I will plant right after wheat harvest, no delay, because that window is short. Cotton I will manage a bit more carefully for insects, but I won’t put too much area into it because our household labor is limited.
